body:
GenNx360 Capital Partners has closed its fourth flagship fund with $865 million in commitments, above target and the biggest fund it has raised. The Fund IV close comes twenty years into a strategy of buying founder- and management-led industrial and business services companies in the lower middle market.

GenNx360 makes control investments in industrial and business services companies in the United States, concentrating on industrial machinery and components, oil and gas, logistics and supply chain, agricultural services, specialty chemicals and aerospace. Like many private equity firms, GenNx360 pairs financial ownership with operating involvement and grows platforms through add-on acquisitions, a pattern visible across its portfolio.

Limited partners in Fund IV include a mix of existing and new investors, including pension plans, asset managers, insurance companies, foundations and family offices. That spread matters in a market where re-up rates have carried most successful raises and a fund that adds new institutional names while holding its existing base is doing something its peers largely are not.

“We are deeply grateful to our long-standing limited partners for their continued trust and partnership, and we are pleased to welcome our new investors to the GenNx360 platform,” said Ron Blaylock , the founder of GenNx360. “Fund IV reflects confidence in our team, our strategy, and the model we have built over nearly two decades of investing in founder- and management-led businesses.”

Fund IV has made five investments to date across infrastructure services, testing and inspection services, aerospace and defense, and IT services. Four have been identified publicly. Industrial pipeline services company Shenandoah Industrial Solutions was acquired in September 2024 ; Heartland Business Systems , a Wisconsin information technology services provider, in October 2025 ; and NVI , a testing, inspection, certification and compliance platform, in February 2026 .

The fourth was not a new platform. GenNx360 has owned aircraft component repair and parts distribution business Precision Aviation Group since 2018 and moved it into a $400 million single-asset continuation fund in November 2023 , led by Neuberger Berman and Blackstone Strategic Partners . Fund IV backed the most recent equity investment in the company alongside that vehicle, and the position was realized in May 2026. A fifth investment, in food services and meal preparation, is expected to close within the next two weeks.

The buy-and-build pattern runs through the portfolio. Shenandoah Industrial Solutions added Pro-Pipe Services in May 2025 and Nu-Pipe in September 2025. Heartland Business Systems acquired Applied Tech Solutions in April 2026. Gear manufacturer Horsburgh & Scott acquired Franklin Machine & Gear in April 2026, and food service company Whitsons Culinary Group acquired Arbor Management in 2024 and Glendale Senior Dining in January 2025.

The fundraise followed a slew of cash-on-cash returns. The sale of Precision Aviation Group to VSE , completed in May 2026 , valued the business at approximately $2.0 billion in cash and equity. GenNx360 sold Aero 3 to VSE for $350 million in January 2026 . In November 2024 , the firm sold information technology reseller ITsavvy to Xerox Holdings for $400 million; in September 2024 , it sold Miller Environmental Group to Coalesce Capital ; and in August 2024 , it sold generator servicer GenServe to Aurora Capital Partners .

“The value our investment approach creates from sourcing to exit is demonstrated by the fact that across our funds we have realized over $1.3 billion in the last 12 months and in excess of $2 billion over the last 2.5 years for our investors,” said Monty Yort , a managing partner of GenNx360.

Those distributions matter in the current fundraising market. Middle market private equity firms raised $94.8 billion in 2025, down more than 40 percent from 2024 and the lowest total since 2020, according to PitchBook . Through the first three quarters of the year, 88 middle market funds had closed on $71 billion.

The problem is fairly simple: limited partners need distributions from older funds to make new commitments, and those distributions have been slow to come. According to PitchBook, no middle market vintage newer than 2016 has yet returned more than its paid-in capital. Bain & Company described the 2026 fundraising market as increasingly split between managers that can point to realized returns and those still asking investors to underwrite marks.

That makes the GenNx360 raise more interesting than the headline number alone. The firm exceeded its target with commitments from both existing and new investors at a time when many managers are spending longer in market. In this environment, cash returned to investors carries a lot more weight than unrealized gains still sitting in the portfolio.

GenNx360 is one of a small number of lower middle market industrial managers to close a flagship above target this year. Align Capital Partners closed its fourth fund at a $770 million hard cap in June alongside a $375 million independent sponsor vehicle, Levine Leichtman Capital Partners closed a $2.0 billion lower middle market fund in July, and Broadwing Capital closed a $440 million debut fund in August. Each raised on realized distributions rather than on paper marks.

GenNx360 was founded in 2006 by Ron Blaylock and manages approximately $3 billion in capital. The firm’s first fund closed in 2008 at more than $500 million, which makes Fund IV roughly 70 percent larger than the vehicle that launched the platform. GenNx360 is headquartered in New York City.
